observations: Historical equipment requests require the controlled actor, bounded queue, newer sequence, matching revision and expected hand/destination before a transfer or world interaction. One queued action is processed per frame; network delivery, lifecycle cleanup and current chronology owners remain open.

Historical topology planning resolves deterministic occupied/empty attachments, checks capacities and fit conflicts before deferred changes, and rejects moving an item with children. A transfer between worn location and hand updates topology and EquipSlot but does not explicitly refresh ArmorItem; whether the protection consumer or another system reconciles it requires a connected current trace.

Historical pickup computes the world item centre by subtracting a local anchor offset from translation, while dropped items are dynamic and their collider contains that local offset. Checkpoint 059 already records a conditional orientation/frame concern; actual current physical transforms, authored offsets and native collision behavior remain independently open.

Historical reconnect removes queued work and rekeys last accepted sequence. Source tests were read but not run; no equipment action, physics query, product build, test, simulation or runtime probe ran.
remaining: Trace current equipment transfer and authoritative protection/appearance state, all supported placement and attachment transitions, sequence/revision admission, pickup coordinate frames, native collider and reconnect lifecycle; reconcile historical aliases and independently assess every lens.
